subproblem.title: The graph-plane projection map is C^2, with derivative at 0 of Hilbert-Schmidt size sqrt 2
subproblem.statement: For natural numbers n, l let Pi : L(R^n, R^l) -> L(R^(n+l), R^(n+l)) send A to the orthogonal projection (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto Gamma_A = span{graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n}, both spaces carrying the operator norm. Then (1) Pi is C^2 (ContDiff R 2), and (2) for every H in L(R^n, R^l), hsNormSq (DPi(0)[H]) = 2 hsNormSq H, where DPi(0) = fderiv R Pi 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ 2 (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection) ∧ ∀ H : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection) 0 H) = 2 * hsNormSq H
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, notation paragraph (J_A v = graphPoint v (A v), J_A^* J_A = I + A^*A, Pi(A) = J_A (I + A^*A)^-1 J_A^*), step 1 (Pi is C^infinity: inversion is smooth on invertible operators) and step 2 (DPi(0)[H] = [[0, H^*],[H, 0]], |DPi(0)[H]|^2 = |H^*|^2 + |H|^2 = 2|H|^2). This is Simon's description (p. 123) of the matrix of p_{T G(f)} as [[I, Df],[Df^t, O]] + F(Df) with F(0) = 0, DF(0) = 0. The adjoint ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch05.Submission, so transposes are built from the standard basis below.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n (i < n); E_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 in R^(n+l) (k in Fin (n+l)); V := (Rn n ->L[R] Rn l), W := (Amb n l ->L[R] Amb n l), both normed by the operator norm; Pi(A) := (span R (range fun v => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection.

0. graphPoint. From graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append x y): its castAdd l i coordinate is x_i and its natAdd n j coordinate is y_j (Fin.append_left/right; all indices are of these forms by Fin.addCases). Hence graphPoint is jointly linear and graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y, where iota x := graphPoint x 0 and kappa y := graphPoint 0 y are continuous linear maps R^n -> R^(n+l) and R^l -> R^(n+l). (Formal route: graphPoint x y = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd.symm (x, y), proved by ext k, Fin.addCases and simp [graphPoint]; then iota := finAddEquivProd.symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inl and kappa := finAddEquivProd.symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inr.) Moreover ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Fin.sum_univ_add), so iota and kappa are isometric; <iota x, kappa y> = 0; <iota x, E_(castAdd i)> = x_i, <iota x, E_(natAdd j)> = 0, <kappa y, E_(castAdd i)> = 0, <kappa y, E_(natAdd j)> = y_j.

1. Transpose. For a continuous linear L : R^n -> R^(n+l) let L^T := sum_{i<n} (innerSL R (L e_i)).smulRight e_i, i.e. L^T w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i. Expanding v = sum_i v_i e_i gives <L^T w, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> v_i = <w, L v> for all v, w. The map tau : L |-> L^T is R-linear (L |-> innerSL R (L e_i) is linear and smulRight is linear in the functional) and continuous (finite dimension). Formally, build tau as a LinearMap with toFun L := sum_i (innerSL R (L e_i)).smulRight e_i and turn it into a continuous linear map with LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap. Hence tau is a continuous linear map and in particular C^infinity.

2. Parametrization. For A in V put J_A := iota + kappa o A (continuous linear R^n -> R^(n+l)); by step 0, J_A v = graphPoint v (A v). The map A |-> J_A is the constant iota plus the continuous linear map A |-> kappa o A (ContinuousLinearMap.compL), so it is C^infinity and has derivative H |-> kappa o H at every point. Since J_A is linear, its range is a subspace, so Gamma_A = span(range J_A) = range J_A (Submodule.span_eq, LinearMap.coe_range). Also ||J_A v||^2 = ||v||^2 + ||A v||^2 >= ||v||^2.

3. Gram operator. G_A := J_A^T o J_A in L(R^n, R^n). By step 1, <G_A v, v> = <J_A v, J_A v> = ||J_A v||^2 >= ||v||^2, so G_A v = 0 forces v = 0. Thus G_A is injective, hence (finite dimension; LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot via ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_toLinearMap) a unit of the complete normed ring L(R^n, R^n). Put R_A := Ring.inverse G_A, so G_A o R_A = R_A o G_A = 1. The map A |-> G_A = tau(J_A) o J_A is C^infinity (composition through the continuous bilinear composition map, ContDiff.clm_comp).

4. Projection formula. Put F(A) := J_A o R_A o J_A^T in W. For w in R^(n+l): F(A) w = J_A(R_A J_A^T w) lies in range J_A = Gamma_A; and for every element J_A v of Gamma_A, <w - F(A) w, J_A v> = <J_A^T w - J_A^T J_A R_A J_A^T w, v> = <J_A^T w - G_A R_A J_A^T w, v> = 0 by step 1 and G_A o R_A = 1. By the characterization of the orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), Pi(A) w = F(A) w. Hence Pi(A) = F(A) for every A, i.e. Pi = F as functions on V. (The Lean proof of the accepted lemma aetp_starProjection_range_continuousOn, commit 9f89be4c, makes the same identification with the same hand-built transpose.)

5. Smoothness (first conjunct). The ring L(R^n, R^n) is complete, so Ring.inverse is C^infinity at each of its units (contDiffAt_ringInverse; the instance HasSummableGeomSeries holds). Every G_A is a unit (step 3) and A |-> G_A is C^infinity, so A |-> R_A is C^infinity at every A (ContDiffAt.comp), hence C^infinity (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Then F, built from the C^infinity maps A |-> J_A, A |-> R_A and A |-> J_A^T = tau(J_A) by composition of operators (ContDiff.clm_comp), is C^infinity, in particular C^2. Since Pi = F (step 4), Pi is C^2.

6. Values at A = 0. J_0 = iota. pi := iota^T satisfies pi w = sum_i <iota e_i, w> e_i = sum_i w_(castAdd i) e_i; in particular pi(iota v) = v, so G_0 = pi o iota = 1 and R_0 = Ring.inverse 1 = 1; moreover pi E_(castAdd i) = e_i and pi E_(natAdd j) = 0.

7. Derivative at 0. Fix H in V. Use the product rule for compositions of operator-valued maps, D(c o d)[H] = Dc[H] o d + c o Dd[H] (HasFDerivAt.clm_comp), and the chain rule.
 (a) DJ(0)[H] = kappa o H, and D(J^T)(0)[H] = tau(kappa o H) = (kappa o H)^T (tau is linear).
 (b) DG(0)[H] = (kappa o H)^T o iota + pi o (kappa o H). Both terms vanish: for v in R^n, (kappa H)^T(iota v) = sum_i <kappa(H e_i), iota v> e_i = 0 and pi(kappa(H v)) = sum_i <iota e_i, kappa(H v)> e_i = 0, because <iota x, kappa y> = 0. So DG(0) = 0 (as a continuous linear map V -> L(R^n, R^n)).
 (c) The derivative of Ring.inverse at the unit 1 is X |-> -(1 X 1) = -X (hasFDerivAt_ringInverse applied to the unit 1 = G_0); by the chain rule DR(0)[H] = -DG(0)[H] = 0.
 (d) Writing F(A) = J_A o (R_A o J_A^T): DF(0)[H] = DJ(0)[H] o R_0 o J_0^T + J_0 o (DR(0)[H] o J_0^T + R_0 o D(J^T)(0)[H]) = kappa o H o pi + iota o (kappa o H)^T.
 Because Pi = F, fderiv R Pi 0 = fderiv R F 0, hence D_H := fderiv R Pi 0 H = kappa o H o pi + iota o (kappa o H)^T. (In block form w.r.t. R^n x R^l this is [[0, H^T],[H, 0]].)

8. Hilbert-Schmidt norm (second conjunct). hsNormSq D_H = sum_{k in Fin (n+l)} ||D_H E_k||^2 = sum_{i<n} ||D_H E_(castAdd i)||^2 + sum_{j<l} ||D_H E_(natAdd j)||^2 (Fin.sum_univ_add).
 - k = castAdd i: pi E_k = e_i and (kappa H)^T E_k = sum_(i') <kappa(H e_(i')), E_(castAdd i)> e_(i') = 0, so D_H E_k = kappa(H e_i) and ||D_H E_k||^2 = ||H e_i||^2 (kappa isometric).
 - k = natAdd j: pi E_k = 0 and (kappa H)^T E_k = sum_(i') <kappa(H e_(i')), E_(natAdd j)> e_(i') = sum_(i') (H e_(i'))_j e_(i'), so D_H E_k = iota(sum_(i') (H e_(i'))_j e_(i')) and ||D_H E_k||^2 = sum_(i') (H e_(i'))_j^2 (iota isometric, coordinates of a vector of R^n).
 Therefore hsNormSq D_H = sum_i ||H e_i||^2 + sum_j sum_(i') (H e_(i'))_j^2 = hsNormSq H + sum_(i') sum_j (H e_(i'))_j^2 = hsNormSq H + sum_(i') ||H e_(i')||^2 = 2 hsNormSq H, exchanging the finite sums and using ||z||^2 = sum_j z_j^2 for z in R^l (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). This is the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y with iota, kappa isometric and mutually orthogonal; J_A = iota + kappa o A parametrizes Gamma_A
Hand-built transpose L^T w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i; the Gram operator G_A = J_A^T J_A >= I is a unit
Pi(A) = J_A G_A^-1 J_A^T by the orthogonality characterization of starProjection; Pi is C^infinity by contDiffAt_ringInverse
At 0: G_0 = 1, DG(0) = 0, D(inverse o G)(0) = 0, so DPi(0)[H] = kappa H pi + iota (kappa H)^T
On the standard basis: hsNormSq DPi(0)[H] = |H|^2 + |H^T|^2 = 2 hsNormSq H
